subject: Reserved capacity request — Vortrix.ai — pricing sensitivity & operational risks
messages:
From: Elena Morris <ops@vortrix.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask + pricing sensitivity for Vortrix

Hi Dev,

Thanks again for the discussion last week. Our execs asked me to pull a short write-up for procurement: Vortrix is evaluating a reserved capacity commit for H2 (primarily inference for our customer-facing agents). We have two constraints that will determine the final ask: budget (capex vs opex split) and exposure to GPU market volatility.

High level: we expect ~1.2M tokens/month steady-state in Q3, with spikes to ~4x during launches. We want a 12–18 month reserved commitment window but would like guardrails if GPU spot/market pricing drops or spikes. Specifically, can Redwood offer: 1) tiered discounts by committed GPU-hours, 2) an indexation clause tying unit price to a published GPU market index, and 3) an operational fallback (partial decommit / burst credits) if we need flexibility during the first 3 months?

Please send a recommended sizing template and the pricing sensitivity scenarios you use (worst / base / best). Also include the SOW template and any standard contract clauses around price-indexation you offer.

Can we lock a 30-min call Wed morning PT to align?

Attachments: Vortrix_RFP.pdf (1 page)

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morris
Head of Ops, Vortrix.ai
ops@vortrix.ai
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <ops@vortrix.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + pricing sensitivity for Vortrix

Thanks, Elena — appreciate the detail. Attaching a short capacity-sizing workbook and a cost-sensitivity sketch (Capacity_Model & CostScenario) that maps committed GPU-hours to per-token economics across three pricing scenarios.

High-level thoughts (quick):
- For your traffic pattern I recommend a baseline reserved pool sized to cover 1.5x steady-state (gives headroom for launches) with a 3-month phased activation to avoid upfront over-provisioning.
- We can offer tiered discounts at commit bands (see workbook). Indexation clauses are possible but need wording that protects both sides; standard approach ties the per-token unit to a monthly published GPU index with a negotiated floor/ceiling.
- Operational fallback: can provide limited burst credits and a one-time partial decommit (up to 20%) within first 90 days with a pro-rated reconciliation. That requires finance sign-off.

I'm looping in Kim (AE) to lead pricing and Laura (revenue manager) for approval path. Can we do Wed 10:00 PT?

Attached: capacity_model_vortrix.xlsx

Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 12:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity ask — Vortrix — pricing guardrails?

Team — forwarding Vortrix ask (attached RFP). Quick summary + recommended approach I want to align on before the Wed call: 

Summary of ask: 12–18 month commit, want tiered discount and indexation clause + ability to partially decommit in first 90 days. Traffic: ~1.2M tokens/month steady, spikes to 4x for launches.

My recommendation (ops + margin-aware):
- Baseline commit: size to 1.5x steady-state = lower risk of burst exposure. Phase activation over 90 days.
- Pricing: propose three-band discount: 10% @ baseline, 18% @ +50% committed, 28% @ +100% committed.
- Indexation: accept indexation only with a negotiated floor (we propose a 10% floor on current unit price) and a 30% ceiling protection for us if GPU spot increases rapidly. Any ask to fully pass through vendor-side GPU price drops needs legal review.
- Decommit/fallback: allow one partial decommit (<=20%) in first 90 days with pro-rated clawback. Offer X hours of burst credits equivalent to 25% of committed baseline for 60 days.

Approvals / escalation: 
- Kim can negotiate up to 20% discount. 
- Laura (you) need to sign off on anything that materially changes margin (discount >20% or indexation without floor).
- Anything >30% discount or more than one decommit event escalates to APAC/NA revenue ops + Finance.

Risks & open items we should prepare for the call: 
- Finance needs the CostScenario model (attached) for margin impact under each GPU-price scenario.
- Legal will want precise language for indexation; if Vortrix pushes full pass-through that is a no-go.
- Operational: need to validate burst routing and canary rollout with infra (ops) — may add 3–5ms latency under certain burst mixes.

Attached: CostScenario_VTX.xlsx, capacity_model_vortrix.xlsx

Please reply with edits/authority if we should present a more aggressive offer.

Dev

Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity ask — Vortrix — pricing guardrails?

Thanks — good framing. Sales thoughts:

- Market context: Vortrix is a strategic mid-market account with strong upsell potential (adaptive agents product). A more aggressive initial discount (20%) in exchange for a firm 12-month commit and an explicit activation schedule should be acceptable.
- I agree we should avoid open-ended indexation; propose a hybrid: quarterly reconciliation tied to a published GPU price index but with a 8–12% floor (customer benefit below floor) and a 25% cap (our protection above cap).
- Operational fallback: offer 10% one-time decommit + 20% burst credit for the first 60 days. That preserves our provisioning economics.

Action items:
1) Finance: Sean, can you validate margin under Kim's proposed 20% discount vs Dev's stepped bands? I need a short yes/no for the call.
2) Laura: please confirm approval threshold for 20% and whether we should route >25% into exec approval.
3) Draft play: I'll assemble a short negotiation playbook (Negotiation_Play.pdf) with concession ladder and ask sizes.

If everyone agrees, I'll present the 20%/activation schedule hybrid indexation on Wed and keep a one-time 10% decommit in reserve.

-Kim
